Dearest Traveler,

I write to you from the quiet northern frontier of Hokkaido, where the earth sleeps beneath a heavy mantle of snow. In the silent birch forests, only the soft crunch of the red-crowned crane’s step breaks the stillness. Here, winter is not a mere season, but a deep spiritual pause. At night, as you submerge into the volcanic warmth of an outdoor onsen, the freezing wind carries the faint scent of sulfur and wild pine, and the starry skies seem close enough to touch.

In the summer, this frozen canvas transforms. The rolling lavender fields of Furano wash the valleys in violet, and the cool mountain air brings the crisp scent of earth reborn. Hokkaido teaches us the beauty of extremes—how the harshest cold prepares the soil for the sweetest bloom.

May your heart find its quiet sanctuary,
Kokoro of the North
